questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The local culture is vibrant and dynamic, and the laboratory, library, and teaching facilities are highly advanced.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I truly enjoyed my exchange experience. The place is full of energy, with a strong academic atmosphere, abundant extracurricular activities, and a vibrant university town nearby.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Both UW–Madison and KU assigned us outgoing study advisors who provided almost all the essential information via email, including guidance on part-time employment. The departments here work efficiently, and it is easy to get help quickly whenever a problem arises.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received several forms of assistance upon arrival. The university provided clear guidance on how to apply for the public transportation card and the campus ID card, as well as support with course selection. There was also an orientation session that helped me understand the campus resources, along with a campus and city travel tour that made it easier to settle into the new environment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The university also sent frequent emails about various cultural exchange activities, language-learning events, and lectures.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding off-campus housing depends largely on the length and timing of your stay. If you are looking for a one-year lease, there are plenty of student apartments available. However, for short-term leases in the fall semester, housing tends to be more competitive, so it’s helpful to email Madison apartment complexes in advance. Options like Dwell, The Towers on State Apartments, and Waterfront Apartments may have availability. For the spring semester, there are usually many sublease offers at discounted prices, so finding housing is generally quite easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Madison is relatively small, and its public transportation system is fairly well developed. However, if you live on the west or east side of the city, you may still need to wait more than 30 minutes for a bus. In contrast, State Street has frequent bus services that allow you to move through campus quickly. The area around State Street is lively and safe, and even at 3 a.m., you can still see many young people out and enjoying themselves.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found my short-term housing on my own, and my property manager was Palisade Property Management. Unfortunately, they were quite unprofessional. They did not take care of the apartment’s condition before I moved in, and they even started renovating the unit during my stay, which forced us to move out.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is easy, there are a course system. You can find all of the available courses, but some courses are limited you need contact teacher to get their approval firstly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Finding all of the course in the system and then choose courses you want to attend. The courses will have requirement you need to meet, so you need to check weather you are available to choose this course. If your are not meet the requirement, the system will notice that you are not available to choose this course and tell you the reason. But you can contact the course's teacher to get approval, they can give you access to choose this course on system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The organization of OutgoingStudy will email all of the time period of choosing courses to you. And they will also send the process of choosing courses to you. So don't worry about collecting information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Actually I was not quite successful when I registered for the classes I wanted. Because almost all of the major course of pharmaceutical are not opened to exchange students, and I must contact course's teacher firstly. Unfortunately, most of teachers told me that we believe you have the ability to complete this course but this course are only opened to degree students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You should contact teacher early and get the approval to choose courses you wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I completed all of my chosen courses successfully and I expanded the thinking aspects although these courses distributed to different fields.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose both advanced level course and graduate level courses. All of the courses are not quite challenging. The course place a strong emphasis on continuous assessment, spreading the academic workload evenly throughout the semester. As long as you follow the study plan consistently, it is quite feasible to achieve good grades.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style are more encouraged and open to talk compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: A A E 335 Intro to Data Analysis; B M I 551 Intro to Biostats for Pop Health; HDFS 516 Family Stress and Resilience; NUTR SCI 203 Introduction to Global Health; PUB AFFR 281 What Works in Health Policy.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: B M I 551 Intro to Biostatsic for Pop Health.  The statistical knowledge taught in this course is systematic and comprehensive, which is more helpful for my future career path.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Language learning, mixed food evening, ball competition, free to gym(swimming, skating, climbing, computer game, spa, meditation), club, blind dancing, card game.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Music party by the lake. Enjoy delicious food, music and light socializing

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to other places. If it's winter, you can go ice fishing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is easy to adjust to the local culture, because the people are hospitable and straight, which means we can get direct feedback from them when we chat. And there are many people from different country, so the social environment is inclusive.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Actually, I do not have much experience in socializing with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many local people have besties in their country, so it is hard to build a deeply relationship with them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: To go disco dancing and pop music.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Contact the tutor in advance to confirm the course.
2. Arrange time reasonably to maintain a balance between study and life.
3. There are two very beautiful gyms in the school. Don't miss them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Feel a different culture and a different teaching atmosphere.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: We met a strong housing management organization, so we had to seek legal assistance in unison.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no
